key_insight: In thin-slice liver CT, DLIR—especially medium strength—generally improved image quality metrics versus ASIR-V while preserving lesion visibility.
clinical_relevance: For liver lesion assessment, DLIR may offer a better balance of noise reduction and edge detail than ASIR-V, potentially supporting clearer interpretation on 2.5 mm CT reconstructions.
method: Retrospective study of 90 abdominal contrast-enhanced CT patients with low- and high-contrast hepatic lesions.
Compared DLIR low/medium/high at 2.5 mm with ASIR-V 50% at 2.5 mm and 5 mm.
Assessed objective metrics (SD, SNR, CNR, ERS) and radiologist subjective scores.
evidence_signal: Across subgroups, DLIR reduced lesion noise and increased SNR/CNR, with DLIR-M often outperforming ASIR-V and showing strong subjective image quality.
watch_item: Findings are based on a single retrospective cohort and image-quality metrics rather than diagnostic accuracy or patient outcomes, so generalization to other scanners or settings is limited.
paper_title: Comparative Study on Image Quality of Deep Learning and Adaptive Statistical Iterative Reconstruction-V in Thin Layer CT of liver Lesions
